mainTopic: אבא שאול's rule about waiting at the תחום, the משנה on a bride's and a מת's needs, רב and שמואל on items a non-Jew brought on שבת, and the start of the משנה on caring for the dead.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining אבא שאול's rule: whatever you may speak about on שבת, you may also wait at the תחום for. It shows that the rule explains the clause about guarding produce, building on שמואל's ruling that one may say 'guard my produce' on שבת. The word כלל adds the case of calling an animal standing outside the תחום. A ברייתא and then a new משנה allow waiting at the תחום for the needs of a bride or a מת. The משנה also rules on flutes and on a coffin or grave that a non-Jew prepared on שבת. רב and שמואל argue about flutes when we don't know where they came from: רב forbids them, and שמואל permits them. The משנה's coffin clause supports שמואל, and a bathhouse ברייתא supports רב, with רבי יהודה's leniency for a small bath explained by the גמרא. The גמרא then explains why the coffin and grave may be used right away, and a new משנה begins on caring for the dead on שבת.

steps.title: If the rule explains the first clause, the wording should be negative
steps.stepSummary: Suppose אבא שאול's rule explains the first clause of the משנה (no waiting at the תחום to hire workers). Then he should have worded it negatively: whatever I may NOT speak about, I may NOT wait for.
steps.simpleTranslation: This wording, 'Whatever I may speak about, I may wait for nightfall for it'? He should have said, 'Whatever I may not speak about, I may not wait for nightfall for it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests אבא שאול's rule against the first clause of the משנה and points out that the wording does not match. The first clause is a prohibition, so a positive rule seems out of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause says אין מחשיכין: you may not wait at the תחום to hire workers, because you may not talk about hiring on שבת. A rule meant to explain that prohibition should be negative: what you can't say, you can't wait for. אבא שאול's rule is worded positively, so it does not seem to fit the first clause.

keyTerms.meaning: waiting at the edge of the תחום for nightfall, so you can go further right after שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse 'מחשיך' with doing any work on שבת. It means standing at the edge of the תחום on שבת so that the moment שבת ends you are already there. The question is whether that waiting is allowed when its purpose is something forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: This phrase: 'Anything that I am permitted to speak about
I am allowed to wait for nightfall for it'?
'Anything that I am not permitted to speak about
I am not allowed to wait for nightfall for it' — is what he should have said!
phrases.notes: Matching the negative style of the first clause, אין מחשיכין.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״כׇּל שֶׁאֲנִי זַכַּאי בַּאֲמִירָתוֹ רַשַּׁאי אֲנִי בַּחֲשִׁיכָתו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's earlier question (on the previous עמוד) about which clause of the משנה אבא שאול is referring to.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that אבא שאול's rule explains the first clause (hiring workers).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prohibition should be explained by a negative rule, but אבא שאול's rule is positive.

steps.title: Suggestion: the rule explains the second clause about guarding
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps אבא שאול's rule refers to the later clause: one may wait at the תחום to guard produce and then bring it home by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the later clause: 'But he may wait for nightfall to guard, and he may bring produce in his hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a new placement: the rule goes on the סיפא, the permissive clause. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא is a permission, so a positively worded rule might fit it better. Guarding is something you may talk about on שבת, so waiting for it should be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the later clause of a משנה

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the later clause:
'But he may wait for nightfall in order to guard
and he may bring produce in his hand'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the placement rejected in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-placing the rule onto a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule explains the first clause (hiring workers).
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule explains the second clause (guarding produce).

steps.title: Even on the second clause, the logic seems to run backwards
steps.stepSummary: If the rule explains the guarding clause, it should be worded the other way: whatever I may wait for, I may speak about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the wording should be: 'Whatever I may wait for nightfall for, I may speak about'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new suggestion. The direction of אבא שאול's reasoning does not seem to match the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא's new point is that waiting to guard is allowed. If אבא שאול were building on that, he should reason from waiting to speech: since I may wait, I may also say it. Instead he reasons from speech to waiting, which looks backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: in waiting for nightfall for it

phrases.english: Then this should read: 'Anything that I am permitted to wait for nightfall for
I am allowed to speak about' — is what he should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״כׇּל שֶׁאֲנִי זַכַּאי בַּחֲשִׁיכָתוֹ רַשַּׁאי אֲנִי בַּאֲמִירָתוֹ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the placement proposed in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing אבא שאול's rule on the סיפא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא's new point is about waiting, so the rule should reason from waiting to speech, not from speech to waiting.

steps.title: אבא שאול argues from שמואל's agreed-upon ruling about speech
steps.stepSummary: The rule does explain the סיפא. אבא שאול builds on the ruling of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, which the תנא קמא also accepts: on שבת one may say 'guard my produce in your תחום and I'll guard yours in mine.' Since that speech is permitted, waiting to guard is permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it refers to the later clause. אבא שאול is building on what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a person may say to his friend, 'Guard my produce in your תחום, and I will guard your produce in mine.' אבא שאול is telling the תנא קמא: Don't you agree that a person may say this? So you must also agree that waiting for it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the rule on the סיפא and explains why it moves from speech to waiting. אבא שאול starts from a point both sides already agree on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speech about guarding is already accepted as permitted, based on שמואל. אבא שאול uses that agreed point to prove the disputed one, waiting at the תחום. Arguing from what is known to what is debated is why the rule goes from speech to waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: really / in truth (keeping the earlier suggestion)
the 2,000-אמה limit one may walk on שבת
the first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that אבא שאול is not presenting a new idea. He is drawing out what follows from a point the תנא קמא already accepts.

phrases.english: Actually, it refers to the later clause,
and Abba Shaul is building on this
that Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
It is permitted for a person to say to his friend
'Guard for me the produce that is in your boundary,
and I will guard for you the produce that is in my boundary.'
And Abba Shaul is saying to the first Tanna:

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא מוֹדֵית דְּמוּתָּר אָדָם לוֹמַר לַחֲבֵירוֹ:
phrases.english: Don't you agree that a person may say to his friend:
'Guard for me the produce in your boundary
and I will guard for you the produce in my boundary'?
phrases.notes: The implied conclusion: so waiting at the תחום to guard is permitted too.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַסֵּיפָא קָאֵי, וְאַבָּא שָׁאוּל אַהָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by explaining why the rule moves from speech to waiting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the agreed premise the rule builds on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule should move from waiting to speech, since the סיפא's new point is about waiting.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule moves from speech (agreed, based on שמואל) to waiting (disputed), as a proof aimed at the תנא קמא.

steps.title: What does the word כלל add?
steps.stepSummary: Granted that אבא שאול's rule is 'whatever I may speak about, I may wait for.' Why does he call it a כלל? What extra case does it come to include?
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, say the rule as 'Whatever I may speak about, I may wait for nightfall for.' But what does calling it a 'כלל' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the meaning of the rule is settled, the גמרא asks what the label כלל adds. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול could simply have given the reason for the guarding case. Calling it a כלל suggests it covers more than the case in the משנה. The גמרא wants to know which extra case that is.

keyTerms.meaning: and say / granted, let it read
what does it come to include?
to wait for nightfall for its sake

phrases.english: And say: 'Anything that I am permitted to speak about —
I am allowed to wait for nightfall for it.'
What does the word 'principle' come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the placement settled, the גמרא turns to the word כלל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra case the word כלל adds.

steps.title: כלל includes calling an animal standing outside the תחום
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not wait at the תחום to bring an animal. But if the animal is standing just outside the תחום, one may call it and it comes. אבא שאול's כלל adds that since calling is permitted, waiting for it is permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes what the רבנן taught: One may not wait at the תחום for nightfall to bring an animal. But if it was standing outside the תחום, he may call it and it comes. אבא שאול stated a כלל: whatever I may speak about, I may wait for nightfall for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The word כלל extends אבא שאול's rule to a new case: an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling an animal is permitted speech on שבת. Under אבא שאול's כלל, that means one may also wait at the תחום for the animal. The general wording reaches beyond the produce case in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: that the רבנן taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול's rule goes from speech to waiting. Whatever you may say on שבת, you may also wait at the תחום for. The word כלל extends it to calling an animal standing outside the תחום.

phrases.english: To include that which the Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַחְשִׁיכִין עַל הַתְּחוּם לְהָבִיא בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: One may not wait for nightfall at the boundary in order to bring an animal.
If it was standing outside the boundary —
he may call it and it comes.
Abba Shaul stated a principle:
Anything that I am permitted to speak about —
I am allowed to wait for nightfall for it.
phrases.notes: So, since calling the animal is permitted, waiting at the תחום for it is permitted too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כלל includes the case of calling an animal standing outside the תחום, which makes waiting for it permitted.

steps.title: Waiting at the תחום for a bride's or a מת's needs, and instructing a messenger
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one may wait at the תחום to take care of the needs of a bride or of a מת, such as bringing a coffin and shrouds. One may also tell a messenger where to go and to pay up to two hundred if he can't find it for one hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may wait for nightfall at the תחום to attend to the needs of a bride and the needs of a מת, to bring him a coffin and shrouds. And one may say to him: 'Go to such-and-such place. If you don't find it there, bring it from such-and-such place. If you don't find it for a מנה, buy it for two hundred.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new law: for a bride or a מת, waiting at the תחום is permitted, and so is giving instructions on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These needs are treated leniently because of their importance (a מצוה need). Not only is waiting allowed, but the messenger may even be told where to go and roughly how much to spend.

keyTerms.meaning: to attend to, take care of

phrases.english: And one may wait for nightfall to attend to the needs of a bride
and to the needs of a corpse
to bring him a coffin and shrouds.
And one may say to him: 'Go to such-and-such place,
and if you do not find it in such-and-such place —
bring it from such-and-such place.'
'If you do not find it for a hundred, bring it for two hundred.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a bride's or a מת's needs, one may wait at the תחום and may give a messenger instructions about place and approximate price.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: no exact price may be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה limits the permission: the messenger may be instructed, as long as no exact sum for the purchase is mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: as long as he does not mention to him the exact amount of the purchase.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא adds a limit to the permission to give instructions on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming an exact price sounds too much like doing business on שבת. General guidance is fine, but stating a precise purchase sum is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the exact sum of a purchase

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַזְכִּיר לוֹ סְכוּם מִקָּח.
phrases.english: Provided that he does not mention to him the sum of the purchase.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: וּבִלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to step 7's permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A messenger may be instructed on שבת, but no exact purchase price may be mentioned.

steps.title: The משנה: waiting at the boundary for a bride or a funeral
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits going to the edge of the תחום at the end of שבת in order to take care of a bride's needs or a מת's needs, like a coffin and shrouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may wait for nightfall at the boundary to take care of the needs of a bride, and the needs of a dead person, to bring him a coffin and shrouds.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that one may walk to the edge of the תחום on שבת and wait there for nightfall, in order to take care of a bride or a funeral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one may not go to the תחום on שבת just to be ready to do weekday business once שבת ends. For a מצוה like helping a bride or burying the dead, it is allowed. This is the same law the ברייתא already brought in step 7, but here it appears as the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Waiting for nightfall (at the edge of the תחום, to set out right after שבת)

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One may wait for nightfall at the boundary
to take care of the needs of a bride,
and the needs of a dead person,
to bring him a coffin and shrouds.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְשִׁיכִין עַל הַתְּחוּם לְפַקֵּחַ עַל עִסְקֵי כַּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה whose first clause matches the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may wait at the תחום to take care of a bride's or a מת's needs.

steps.title: Flutes brought by a non-Jew on שבת
steps.stepSummary: If a non-Jew brought flutes on שבת for a funeral, a Jew may not use them for the eulogy, unless they came from a nearby place.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-Jew who brought flutes on שבת: a Jew may not eulogize with them, unless they came from a nearby place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on flutes a non-Jew brought on שבת for a funeral. A Jew may not use them, unless they were brought from nearby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the flutes were carried from outside the תחום, they were brought in a forbidden way, so a Jew may not benefit from them. If they came from inside the תחום ('a nearby place'), nothing forbidden was done, so they may be used. The phrase 'nearby place' is what the גמרא will soon ask about.

phrases.english: A non-Jew who brought flutes on Shabbat:
a Jew may not eulogize with them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן בָּאוּ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב.
phrases.english: unless they came from a nearby place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another funeral-related case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flutes a non-Jew brought on שבת may not be used for a eulogy unless they came from a nearby place.

steps.title: A coffin or grave made by non-Jews on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: If non-Jews made a coffin and dug a grave on שבת, a Jew may be buried in it. If it was made for a Jew, he may never be buried in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they made him a coffin and dug him a grave, a Jew may be buried in it. But if it was for a Jew, he may never be buried in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with non-Jews who made a coffin or dug a grave on שבת. It may be used for a Jew, unless it was made for a Jew in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the non-Jews did the work for themselves (for a non-Jew), a Jew may later use it. If the work was done for a Jew, it is forbidden forever, as a penalty, so that people will not ask non-Jews to work for them on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of a Jew

steps.confusionAlert: 'Never' does not mean only on שבת. Even after שבת, that particular Jew may never be buried in a coffin or grave made for him on שבת.

phrases.english: If they made him a coffin
and dug him a grave,
a Jew may be buried in it.
But if it was for a Jew,
he may never be buried in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשׂוּ לוֹ אָרוֹן וְחָפְרוּ לוֹ קֶבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the משנה. Its wording is used later (step 15) as support for שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coffin or grave a non-Jew made on שבת may be used for a Jew, unless it was made for a Jew.

steps.title: What counts as a nearby place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'from a nearby place' in the flutes case.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'from a nearby place'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a short clarifying question about the flutes case. This sets up the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not 'what is close?' in distance. It is how sure we must be that the flutes came from inside the תחום. Must we know it for certain, or is it enough that it is possible?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
What is 'from a nearby place'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a phrase in the משנה's flutes clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What level of certainty 'from a nearby place' requires.

steps.title: רב: it must truly be from nearby
steps.stepSummary: רב says the flutes may be used only if we know they came from a place that is truly nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: from a place that is truly nearby.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. The flutes may be used only when we know for sure they came from within the תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'nearby' means known to be nearby. If we are unsure where the flutes came from, they are forbidden. In a case of doubt, רב is strict.

phrases.english: Rav said:
from a place that is truly nearby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a known nearby source permits the flutes. When there is a doubt, they are forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל: maybe they stayed just outside the wall
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that even if we don't know where the flutes came from, we assume they may have spent the night just outside the city wall, which is inside the תחום, so they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: we take into account that perhaps they spent the night outside the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second, more lenient answer. If we are unsure where the flutes came from, we may use them, since they may have been kept just outside the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just outside the wall is still inside the תחום, so bringing them from there broke no law. Because of this possibility, a doubt is treated leniently. They are forbidden only if we know they came from beyond the תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: First-generation Babylonian אמורא, often disputing רב

steps.confusionAlert: Here חָיְישִׁינַן leads to a leniency, not a stringency. The 'worry' that the flutes stayed near the wall is what permits them.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
we take into account that perhaps
they spent the night outside the wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא חוּץ לַחוֹמָה לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's answer in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When there is a doubt, the flutes are permitted, since they may have stayed inside the תחום.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The coffin clause permits use when it is unclear who it was made for. So in the flutes case too, a doubt should be permitted, as שמואל says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is precise like שמואל, for it teaches: 'If he made him a coffin and dug him a grave, a Jew may be buried in it.' Evidently, in a case of doubt it is permitted. Here too, in a case of doubt it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a careful reading of the משנה supports שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coffin clause allows burial whenever we don't know that it was made for a Jew. That shows the משנה treats a doubt leniently. The same should apply to the flutes, which is exactly שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is precise (and supports a view)

phrases.english: The Mishnah's wording is precise like Shmuel,
for it teaches:
"If he made him a coffin and dug him a grave,
a Jew may be buried in it."
Evidently, in a case of doubt it is permitted;
here too, in a case of doubt it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for שמואל's view in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a doubt is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The coffin and grave clause of the משנה, which permits use when it is unclear who it was made for.

steps.title: A bathhouse ברייתא supports רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on a bathhouse heated on שבת in a mixed city. With a non-Jewish majority, one may bathe right after שבת. With a Jewish majority or a half-and-half city, one must wait. The strict ruling for half-and-half supports רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא was taught like רב: A city where Jews and non-Jews live, and there is a bathhouse in it that operates on שבת: if the majority are non-Jews, in the evening one may bathe in it immediately. If the majority are Jews, one must wait the time it takes for water to heat. If it is half and half, it is forbidden, and one must wait the time it takes for water to heat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב. It does not explain the proof, so the learner must see it in the half-and-half case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a non-Jewish majority, we assume the water was heated for non-Jews, so it is permitted. With a Jewish majority, it was heated for Jews, so one must wait. In the half-and-half case, we don't know who it was heated for, and the ברייתא forbids it. That shows a doubt is treated strictly, as רב says.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in support of him
The time it would take to heat (the water)

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא brings support for both sides: the משנה for שמואל and a ברייתא for רב. That shows the question of how to treat a doubt here is a real, lasting מחלוקת.

phrases.english: And a Baraita was taught like Rav:
A city where Jews and non-Jews live,
and there is a bathhouse in it
that operates on Shabbat:
if the majority are non-Jews,
in the evening one may bathe in it immediately.
If the majority are Jews,
one must wait the time it takes for water to heat.
If it is half and half,

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר וְיַמְתִּין עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּחַמּוּ חַמִּין.
phrases.english: it is forbidden, and one must wait the time it takes for water to heat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Balances step 15 by bringing a source that supports רב instead of שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that a doubt is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's half-and-half case, where it is unclear who the water was heated for, and bathing is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a small bath with an official present
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that a small bath may be used right away if there is an official authority in the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: in a small bath, if there is an authority there, one may bathe in it immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה's added leniency for a small bath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small bath can be heated very quickly. If there is a powerful person in the city, the water may have been heated for him right after שבת, not on שבת itself. So one need not wait. The next two steps explain what רשות means.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
in a small bath,
if there is an authority there,
one may bathe in it immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dissenting leniency within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small bath may be used right after שבת if a powerful person is in the city, since it may have been heated quickly for him after שבת.

steps.title: What does 'an official authority' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה meant by 'רשות' in his ruling about the small bath.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'רשות'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'רשות' means in רבי יהודה's ruling from the last step. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allowed a small bath to be used right away if there is a 'רשות' in the city. The word is unclear. Is it a government, a ruler, or something else? The גמרא wants to know exactly what case lets us assume the bath was heated after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: An authority or powerful figure. Here it means an important person in the city.
What is? Used to ask for the meaning of a word.

phrases.english: What is 'a ruling power'?
phrases.notes: Asks about the word in רבי יהודה's statement from Step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key word in רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'רשות' in the small bath ruling.

steps.title: An important person with ten servants
steps.stepSummary: 'רשות' means an important person whose ten servants can heat a small bath all at once. So the bath may have been heated after שבת, and a Jew may bathe right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב יצחק the son of רב יהודה: If there is an important person in the city who has ten servants, and they heat ten kettles for him at once into a small bath, it is permitted to bathe in it right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'רשות' means a powerful person whose servants can heat a small bath very quickly. Because of him, we may bathe right after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we wait after שבת for the time it takes to heat the bath, in case it was heated on שבת. But a small bath can be filled in moments when ten servants each pour a kettle at once. So it is possible the bath was heated after שבת for this person, and there is no reason to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: Kettles or jugs used to heat water.

steps.whatToRemember: The small bath is permitted right away only because an important person's servants could heat it in a moment after שבת. So there is no need to suspect it was heated on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda said:
If there is in it (the city) an important person
who has ten servants

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמְּחַמְּמִין לוֹ עֲשָׂרָה קוּמְקוּמִין בְּבַת אַחַת
phrases.english: who heat for him ten kettles at once
in a small bath —
it is permitted to bathe in it immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'רשות' is an important person whose ten servants can heat a small bath at once, so it may have been heated after שבת.

steps.title: Why no waiting time for the coffin and grave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a coffin and grave made by non-Jews. It asks why a Jew may be buried in them right away instead of waiting the time it takes to make them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They made him a coffin and dug him a grave, etc.' Why? Here too, he should wait the time it would take to make them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a coffin and grave that non-Jews made on שבת. It challenges the ruling that a Jew may use them right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the bath in the ברייתא, we wait after שבת for the time the work would take (כדי שיחמו), so that we gain nothing from work done on שבת. So the גמרא asks: why doesn't the same waiting rule (בכדי שיעשו) apply to the coffin and the grave?

keyTerms.meaning: The amount of time it would take to make them.

phrases.aramaic: עָשׂוּ לוֹ אָרוֹן וְחָפְרוּ לוֹ קֶבֶר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'They made him a coffin and dug him a grave, etc.'
Why (is it permitted)?
Here too, let him wait the time it takes for them to be made!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? הָכָא נָמֵי יַמְתִּין בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bath discussion and goes back to the משנה's coffin clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a Jew may be buried right away in a coffin or grave made by non-Jews.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere we wait the time the work would take. That rule should apply here too.

steps.title: The grave is on a public road
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the grave is on a public road. Jews are not buried there, so it was clearly made for a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The case is where it stands on a public road.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge. The משנה is talking about a grave dug on a main public road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jews were not buried on public roads. So a grave there was clearly dug for a non-Jew and not for a Jew. Since everyone can see this, there is no need to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the challenge here.
A main public road or street.

phrases.english: Ulla said: (It is) where it stands on a public road.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to allow any coffin or grave right away, which clashes with the waiting rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a grave on a public road, which was clearly made for a non-Jew.

steps.title: That works for a grave, but what about a coffin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that עולא's answer explains the grave but not the coffin.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works well for a grave. But for a coffin, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's answer. A grave's location shows who it was for, but a coffin has no fixed location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being on a public road proves a grave was made for a non-Jew. But a coffin can be carried anywhere. Its place proves nothing about who it was made for. So the waiting question comes back for the coffin.

keyTerms.meaning: That works well. Used to accept one part before asking about another.
What is there to say? Means: how do you explain this?

phrases.english: That works well for a grave;
a coffin, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח קֶבֶר, אָרוֹן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the limit of עולא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's answer about the public road, as applied to the coffin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Where a grave is located can show who it was for, but a coffin is movable, so its place proves nothing.

steps.title: The coffin was placed on a non-Jew's grave
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the coffin was already lying on a non-Jew's grave. That proves it was made for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The case is where it was lying on his grave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the challenge about the coffin. The משנה is talking about a coffin already placed on the non-Jew's grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the coffin sits on the grave of the non-Jew, it is clear it was made for him and not for a Jew. So, just like the grave on the public road, there is no need to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer about the coffin.

steps.whatToRemember: The coffin and grave in the משנה may be used right away because it is clear they were made for a non-Jew. The grave is on a public road, and the coffin lies on the non-Jew's grave.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בְּמוּטָל עַל קִבְרוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: (It is) where it was placed on his grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בְּמוּטָל עַל קִבְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A movable coffin gives no sign of who it was made for.
steps.terutzMaskana: The coffin was already placed on the non-Jew's grave, which shows it was made for him.

steps.title: New משנה: caring for the dead on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that on שבת one may do all the needs of the dead. One may smear and rinse the body without moving its limbs, and slide out the pillow to lay the body on sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may do all the needs of the dead. We may anoint and rinse the body, as long as we do not move any limb. We may slide the pillow out from under it, and lay it on the sand in order to...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists what may be done for a dead body on שבת. This passage ends in the middle of the sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead body is מוקצה on שבת, so it may not be moved directly. The משנה still allows caring for it by smearing oil and rinsing, as long as no limb is moved. One may also pull the pillow out so the body drops onto cool sand. That moves the body only indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: The needs of the dead, meaning care of the body.
We smear oil on the body.
Move, as in moving a limb.

steps.confusionAlert: Pulling the pillow out is allowed even though the body ends up shifting. This is because the body is moved only indirectly and is not lifted by hand. This is different from moving a limb directly, which is forbidden.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
We perform all the needs of the dead:
we smear it with oil and rinse it,
provided that one does not move any limb of it.
We slide the pillow out from under it,
and lay it on the sand in order to
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one may care for a dead body, including smearing and rinsing it, without moving its limbs. One may also slide out the pillow to lay it on sand.
